notes: Rules are bartender fundamentals validated (not derived) from data. data_confidence is the fraction of signal-matching recipes that followed the expected technique; low values reflect corpus noise (shots, hot drinks, punches share signals but differ in technique). PROVISIONAL — Ari to review rule priorities and rationale text.

rules.rationale: Egg white requires a dry shake (no ice) first to build foam, then a second shake with ice to dilute and chill.
rules.notes: data_confidence reflects % of egg-white recipes with 'shake' in instructions; the dry-shake phase is often omitted from written recipes but is the correct bar technique.

rules.rationale: Spirit + carbonated lengthener is built over ice — shaking destroys fizz.

rules.carbonation_note: Muddle herbs gently with citrus and sweet in the glass; add spirit; fill with ice; top with carbonation.
rules.rationale: Muddled-herb carbonated builds (Mojito and other muddled mint-and-soda drinks): gentle muddling releases essential oils without bitterness; shaking after muddling bruises the herbs and clouds the drink.

rules.carbonation_note: Shake spirit + acid + sweet; strain over fresh ice; top with carbonation.
rules.rationale: Sour-highball builds (Collins, Fizz): shake the base, then top with soda or sparkling wine — never shake after adding carbonation.
rules.notes: This trigger sits above plain 'has_acid' to ensure Collins/Fizz builds get highball service rather than coupe.

rules.rationale: Cream + citrus requires vigorous shaking to emulsify the dairy and integrate the acid (cream sours).

rules.ice_note: A large single ice cube keeps dilution slow while chilling the cream — preferred over cracked/cubed for White Russian-style builds.
rules.rationale: Cream without acid is built over ice when it's a long sipper (White Russian) — no emulsification needed.
rules.ambiguity_note: Cream-without-acid splits two ways: build over ice for long sippers (White Russian), or shake and serve up for dessert cocktails (Brandy Alexander, Grasshopper). Default here is build; if the drink is a frothy dessert cocktail, shake it and serve up instead.
rules.notes: 'Cream' in many classic recipes means half-and-half (half milk, half cream), not pure heavy cream; either works for the build method.

rules.rationale: Citrus juice requires shaking to integrate, aerate, and dilute.
rules.notes: data_confidence includes shots, hot drinks, and punches in the denominator — purely cocktail data would score higher.

rules.rationale: Fresh herbs are muddled gently to release essential oils; the drink is then built over crushed ice (Mint Julep: bourbon, mint, sugar).
Spirit-forward builds (Old Fashioned, Negroni, Manhattan) are stirred for clarity and gentle, controlled dilution — no acid to emulsify.
rules.notes: Service is rocks by default. The host may suggest 'up' (coupe) for spirit+vermouth builds in the Martini/Manhattan family — the template context (Spirit+Vermouth vs Spirit-Forward) informs that call.

rules.rationale: Build over ice when no specific technique signal is present.
